en: In the fourth month of summer, the first year of the Jingding era, the monk Zhengbin of Mount Jing brought a volume tucked under his arm and visited me, saying:
"It has been six years since our teacher, Chan Master Shixi Fohai, passed away. His disciples have recorded his words and prepared them for carving into woodblocks, yet they lack a preface.
Without this, there will be no means to ensure their transmission to posterity. Only you, sir, truly know our teacher."
"Profound! I pray that you will grant me this request. At this, I was moved by a private reflection.

When Master Zhu Wen Gong first went to Yanping to inquire about the Way, the only items he carried in his satchel were a single volume of the *Mencius* and a collection of the *Recorded Sayings of Dahui*.

Although the Master was extremely rigorous in refuting heterodox teachings, he nonetheless held these two works in such singular esteem and faith. Could this possibly have been so without some profound insight?
How extraordinary! While Qin Hui was wielding power over the state, from the high ministers and officials down to the great officers, none dared to oppose or offend him.

Yet Daoyue, a mere monk clad in a single robe, was able to invoke the great principle of avenging the nation and speak out without restraint. He even said to Qin Hui: "Cao Cao held the Son of Heaven to command the empire;
today you hold the barbarians to command the Son of Heaven. Though his own person was subjected to exile to the south...
His fame shook the realm, placing him on equal footing with figures such as Zhang Hengpu and Hu Zhongjian.
I have privately examined his writings, and their essential words and refined principles often accord with those of Mencius.

That which Mencius called "being unable to be moved by poverty or low status, and unable to be bent by force or intimidation"—Daohui possessed this quality. It was precisely for this that Master Wen took him up.
This [land] belongs here and not there. When Shixi was at Jiangshan, there was a son of the Wang family who was actually a descendant of Wang Anshi.
Relying on the influence of powerful officials, he sought to seize land within the mountains to establish a burial field. Shixi contested this, but was unsuccessful.
Thereupon, he beat the drums loudly, recited a verse, and departed. He thought to himself: "This man was one from a previous generation who deluded the world with his learning.

If I were to comply with his request, would I not alone be laughed at by the spirits of the mountains? He then proceeded toward East Zhejiang, traveling extensively through its fine mountains and waters, intending to spend the remainder of his life there.
From that time on, his reputation became preeminent in his day; it was known not only by the various officials of the gentry.

The Sage Emperor was also aware of this; he presided over the famous mountain, bestowed upon it an auspicious title, and his majestic grace shone forth brilliantly, no different from the fortune encountered by Dahui.
Alas! The fierce flames of the wicked Qin Gui were feared by the whole world, yet Dahui was able to resist them.
Wang Anshi’s lingering influence still held sway over those in power, yet Shixi was able to oppose it.
Although the effort required for each may have differed in difficulty, their extraordinary vision and noble insight were as if from one and the same person.
Were it not for intelligence, talent, learning, and a discernment of principle—who could have achieved this? Thus, this compilation shall circulate alongside the *Recorded Sayings* of Dahui.

It is permissible to do so regarding worldly matters. As for transmitting the ancestral robe of Songyuan, continuing the orthodox lineage of Yangqi, expounding the eighty-four thousand verses, and discussing the thirty-two principles of the Dharma—these are matters beneath the *kāṣāya* that are beyond my knowledge.
I have merely selected those instances that transcend common custom and provide benefit to the teachings of the world, setting them forth and placing them at the beginning of this work.
This preface also embodies the lingering intent of Master Zhu (Zhuzi). The Master was a native of Meishan; his name was Xin Yue and his surname was Wang.
It is said that his family had followed the scholarly tradition of Confucianism for generations.

This preface was composed on the full moon of the seventh month of this year by Liu Zhensun of Bohai, Grand Officer of the Central Palace, Junior Minister of the Court of Imperial Kinship, concurrently Compiler of the National History Institute and Editor of the Veritable Records Institute.

The Recorded Sayings of Master Shixi, Volume One:
The Recorded Sayings of Chan Master Fohai of Shixi upon His Initial Appointment at Ba’en Chan Temple in Jiankang Prefecture,
Compiled by Attendant Zhu Xian.

"Entering the hospital" refers to the three gates. One does not stand in isolation or peril; one does not sit upon the level ground. There is a path for turning the body, and every step transcends the ordinary.
While you are precisely outside the Gate of Gratitude, how can you enter this Gate of Gratitude? He lets out a shout.
The Buddha Hall: the Buddhas of the past and the Buddhas of the future, the single body and the manifold bodies—all are gathered here. Inserting incense, he says: "Take this as proof.

Occupying the abbot’s seat, one remains unchanging through a hundred refinements; struck once with the hammer, it is complete. Is this not like working upon a dull and stubborn furnace? How does one apply the technique?
To perceive the profound mystery and the steep, sharp edge of the spiritual pivot is precisely what a skilled physician does for a terminal ailment. How does one administer the medicine? New.
Repaying kindness. Though I am neither a forge nor a skilled physician, we have met by chance upon a narrow path. [The Master] strikes the meditation seat and says:

"I cannot let you off. He holds up the notice: "The Emperor’s decree within the realm; the General’s command beyond the borders. Even when Buddhas and Patriarchs appear, they must still beg for their lives."
"How is cooperation today? [The Master] hands the *dùtié* (ordination certificate) to the Rector, saying, "Distribute it according to the tally.
He takes up the memorial: "This whole, unbreakable phrase is like wind blowing over water; naturally, it forms patterns. Nevertheless..."
Be absolutely careful not to seek realization in the place where words flow like surging waves.
Take up the Dharma robe; don a cowhide; roll along with the herd of blind donkeys; trailing through water and mud, falling eastward and tumbling westward.
At Huangmei, seven hundred people could not understand it.
He pointed to the Dharma seat and said, "This seat is high and broad; I am unable to ascend it.

While a failure on the part of Śāriputra might still be excusable, if a Buddha, a Patriarch, or a great teacher of the world were to ascend this seat and fail, the deficiency would be all the more grave.
Today, I cannot help but strip away his very roots. He then ascended the seat, held up the incense, and said, "This single offering of incense is respectfully for..."
For the present Emperor, may his sacred life be prolonged: ten thousand years, ten thousand years, ten thousand times ten thousand years! Next, holding up the incense, he says:

"This one portion of incense is offered for the sake of the Great Minister, the Commissioner of the Regional Administration, and all the officials of the various bureaus, to augment their years of official service.
Next, holding up the incense, he says: "This one portion of incense is offered for the sake of..."
Formerly he resided at Yunju, and later he resided at Zijin. He closed his room to honor the late Great Master, thereby repaying the kindness of the Dharma-milk.
Then, taking his seat, he said: "In the past, I held fast; the lives of all people were in the hands of Venerable Yue.
Today, I let go; the life of Venerable Yue is in the hands of all people. Is there anyone who will not let go?"
The guest asked, "How so? A monk asked, "Having temporarily ceased your duties as the head of the monastery at Mount Zhongshan, you have come to ascend this dharma site at Baen Temple.
The fourfold assembly has all gathered; we wish to hear the essentials of the Dharma. The Master said, "To the east of Shicheng and to the west of Yecheng.

The monk pressed further, "The great assembly is delighted; where shall they go? The Master said, "Today, there is no room for expedient means. The monk asked, "What is the primary phrase? The Master said, "Great."
The ground bears it up without arising. The monk asked, "What is the final word? The Master said, "With my guts turned upside down and my bowels emptied out, to whom could I speak it?
The monk asked, "This word was attained at Yunju; it was attained at Yunding. The Master said, "The hollow speculations of floating life are irrelevant.
The monk bowed. The Master said, "The past has already passed; the future has not yet arrived. It is precisely the present moment."
Regarding the principle of the single transmission at Vulture Peak and the school of direct pointing at Shaolin: is there a place where it is entrusted?
Is there a portion to be borne? If there is, then the seal of the Western Patriarch has not been transmitted to this land;
if there is not, then today this assembly sits and stands with solemn dignity. Although the Elder Yue has turned his play-clothes inside out to enter this theater of drama, nevertheless—
If one does not strike the drums and pipes, is there anyone who can discern and clarify this? Come forth and take up the burden across your shoulders;
overturn this entire arena at once! If you wish to see the Buddha-dharma and receive its transmission, even if you act in such a manner, I have not yet nodded my head in approval for you.
Why? "One hundred and fifty [blows]—I find it hard to let you go. Again, he cited Shoushan: "And..."
Shang addressed the assembly, saying: "The Buddha-dharma is entrusted to kings and great ministers. But tell me, what is it that is entrusted?
It must be to our elder brother Kāśyapa that this is possible. The Master remarked: "Shoushan’s proclamation in this manner is much like a heavy object falling where it naturally gravitates."

Little do they realize that what was entrusted to the kings and ministers five hundred years ago was already spoken by those at Shengyuan Pavilion and in the Imperial Street, such that the harmony throughout the four quarters of the world was radiant and pervasive. But tell me, what was it that was said?
It must have been an elder like Shoushan who could truly understand.

That evening, there was a small informal sermon (*xiaochan*). The questions and answers are not recorded. The Master said: "Existence is non-existence; non-existence is existence. Twist the nostrils and the eyes;

as soon as you intend to act thus, it is already not thus. It completely changes the heart, liver, and five viscera; it bites through the duality of departing and abiding; it tears asunder past and present.
Thus, naturally, even in the bustling streets and alleys of flowers and willows, there is the ancestral style of the ancient Buddhas."
In the quiet chambers of an ancient temple, when all is cold and still, the livelihood of a practitioner is such that like voices respond to one another and like breaths seek one another out.
Raising the eyebrows, the face is right here before you. It is just as when a monk asked Caoshan, "How was it before the Buddha appeared in the world?
Caoshan said, "Caoshan is not as good. [The monk asked,] "And how was it after he appeared in the world? [Caoshan said,] "Not as good as Caoshan. Now tell me, what about after he appeared?
Before he appeared in the world, where did the discrepancy between the "as it is" and the "not as it is" lie?

You who are well-able to refine and polish—utter a single phrase and rescue the new Elder! Is there anyone who can? After a long silence, he said: "Because of often seeing someone off, I remember the moment of parting from my family.
Again, he raised an instance: Master Bao sent someone to deliver a message to Dashi: "Why do you not go down the mountain to teach and transform the masses?"
"Born. [The Master] looked up at the Milky Way and asked, "What is this? Sida said, "The Buddhas of the three periods have all been swallowed by me in a single gulp;

what sentient beings are there to teach? The Master said, "Sida, atop a solitary peak, considered himself quite extraordinary, yet when someone on the crossroads struck him with a flying tile, he was turned over along with his whole body. He wished—
Do you understand? It was not merely intended to strike the grass; it was also meant to startle the snakes.
When Daoju arrived, he ascended the hall and, raising his whisk, said: "Of the high mountains and flowing waters, those who strike the right note are rare.

Of the sparks of flint and flashes of lightning, those who can keep pace are few. He then placed the whisk back in its original position and said: "The old friends of Cudao Monastery must not be forgotten."
People! To bring it all together is nothing but a field of shame. On the eighth day of the twelfth lunar month, he ascended the hall and said:
"The Formerly Enlightened One practiced austerities for six years; on the eighth day of the twelfth month, when the morning star appeared, he attained Equal and Perfect Enlightenment.
After a long silence, he said: "An eighty-year-old old man rolls a brocade ball, heedless of his entire body being covered in mud and water."

At the Yuan Dynasty court, he ascended the hall. Holding up his staff, he said: "The new year begins, and all things are renewed. As for this mountain-shaped staff, it remains thus, black and wrinkled.
When the time comes, it knows how to laugh and turn itself over. He struck the ground with the staff and said: "I have emptied my belly and poured out my heart to speak for you;
to sing this song, one must be a man from the Imperial Capital."
Ascending the hall: Half of the first month has already passed. Limping and dragging along—have you attained resonance yet?
If you say that speaking with the mouth hits the mark, or that taking a step naturally treads upon it, even a three-year-old child knows how to speak thus.
But as for this single phrase that unifies all paths and follows the same track—how is it? Principle is able to subdue the leopard.
The Memorial Service for the Venerable Master Yan Shi. Burning incense, he said: "A single phrase from Mount Ou is densely arrayed before sound.

To hesitate in thought or pause the mechanism is to be driven out by a hot shout. To see the former master here is not yet to know the former master; to know the former master is not yet to see the former master."
"Now I must see my former teacher. Do you recognize my former teacher? [He] inserts incense and says: "My former teacher passed away long ago. Ascending the hall, he says:

"By naturally restricting one's diet, all illnesses diminish; yet being full of emotion cannot avoid occasional weariness. Living in poverty, every movement results in either opposition or compliance;
one can only attain the single flavor of pure leisure. [The assembly asks: "What is the matter with Baolin today? [He replies: "Why is it that..."
The Patriarch Yun said, "I have finished speaking. He struck the meditation seat and said, "A fine day for many to share. He ascended the hall and said:
"Before the fifteenth day, one knows there is the Way but cannot attain it; one dwells at the house by the fragrant grasses' crossing, yet the body is in the village of apricot blossoms.
After the fifteenth day, one can speak of the Way but does not know it exists; when one family has business, a hundred families are busy. The river...
Losing money in the river, one must fish for it in the river. It is precisely the fifteenth day; the sky is bright and the air clear, the gentle breeze is harmonious and pleasant.
May the Head Seat and the great assembly each enjoy ten thousand blessings. The Western neighbor is already wealthy yet worries about being insufficient;
the Eastern elder, though poor, finds joy in abundance. The hornless iron ox sleeps soundly; throughout one’s life, there is no need for silent sighs of lamentation.
Ascending the hall, he said: "All day long in a state of bustle—yet that matter is not hindered. What is that matter? If you understand it, entering hell will be like an arrow shot;
if you do not understand it either, all day long you will be in a state of bustle, yet that matter remains unhindered."
The Buddha Ascends the Hall on His Birthday: A boulder from the city of Liancheng is fundamentally without flaw; why, upon birth, does it immediately scatter sand?
The lame monk knows where it falls; a good enemy has an evil enemy.
Ascending the hall for the Summer Retreat on the fifteenth day of the fourth month:

Here at a certain ancient temple west of the city of Jiankang, I, together with the present assembly of disciples—whether holy or ordinary, sentient or insentient—with this whisk, I draw a circle and say:

We all dwell here together in the summer retreat, observing the *śīla* (prohibitions) at all times, whether in brothels or wine shops, at fish markets or poultry stalls, appearing and disappearing as we please.
Relaxed and at ease, moving freely in all directions. If this were not so, you would merely be dreaming within a ghost cave.
Entering the hall, he made a single stroke with his hand and said: "With one stroke it is cut off. Right now, eye to eye—can this be called 'sleeping talk'?
And as for what has yet to come, how can you speak of it? Have you ever seen it in a dream?"
"Not yet. Try to examine it with your whole being. Thirty years from now, you will open your eyes and find yourself bed-wetting;
do not be negligent. He ascended the hall and said: "The golden crow flies and the jade hare runs; if you cannot see through the affairs before your eyes, ten days will pass as if they were five."
He gave a shout and said: "Who dares to cough?

He ascended the hall and spoke with clarity and precision, without a single drop of leakage; yet one might not necessarily be able to act upon it. One may act with continuous and dense consistency, without the slightest interruption;
yet one might not necessarily be able to speak of it. To reach the point where speaking and acting coincide—*tu!* Alas, I regret my lack of caution!
At the beginning, when Xie Zhi entered the hall, he remained for one hundred and twenty days. When ninety days had passed, whether this matter was attained or not, set it aside for a moment.
Though it is said to be at the gateway of a bustling marketplace, has the staff ever been moved? Fellow practitioners.

Shoulders meeting. Both word and meaning are complete. Salt is expensive, rice is cheap; the temple master knows this himself. One hand turns up like clouds, the other hand turns down like rain—yet upon whose portion does it fall?
After a long silence, he said: "Every slice of my sincere heart."
Ascending the hall, he said: "No front or back, yet there are apertures; they turn toward one another in intimacy, yet turn away in agitation. The Phoenix Terrace is level, the Stone City is small.
He gave a shout and said: "A solitary lamp beneath the sun—truly, it fails to illuminate."
Ascending the hall at the conclusion of the summer retreat: This is my first year as the abbot of Baoen Temple. The morning gruel and evening meal have been coarse and meager;
I lack the strength to concern myself with the matters of right and wrong, gain and loss, on Vulture Peak twenty centuries ago.
I see only that on the sixteenth day of the sixth month and the twelfth day of the seventh month, great winds and rain blew from the northeast, driving up the tide and causing destruction.
The damage was extensive. Only to the west of the city was the terrain slightly higher, where there was no moisture at all.
He then called out in a loud voice, "Venerable Elders, watch your step!"
Xie Daoniu ascended the hall to pay his respects to an old acquaintance. The Master said, "There is a gentleman within the gate; a gentleman arrives at the gate.
Mazu of Jiangxi, however, said, "Six ears do not share a secret. "When we meet, we do not dismount from our horses; each goes on their own way.
Zhaozhou also said, "The Daoist presents a lacquer vessel. Though one may usually debate like a cascading torrent, here it is difficult to clear one's name. Why is this so?
The assembly was entirely composed of guests from Jiangnan. Opening the furnace, he ascended the hall and said:

A monk asked Master Yexian, "I have come from afar to seek the wind of your teaching; I beg the Master for a reception. Yexian held up a pair of tongs with burning coals and showed them to him, asking, "Do you understand?
The monk said, "I do not understand. Yexian said, "In the furnace, adding more charcoal, one still complains it is cold; on the road..."
"The practitioner merely guards against the cold. The Master said, "What a fine brazier of embers! If you lightly touch it, a blazing fire erupts.
Today, the incense spoon and fire tongs have been handed over all at once. At the depth of night, with a single shove, they will burn away your very face."
Do not say that I have not spoken.
On the occasion of the Longevity Festival, I ascend the hall: prior to the time of Vipaśyin, beyond the kalpa of emptiness, before any sign of news had emerged, the true essence was fully manifest.
All supreme excellence and auspiciousness are contained herein. What serves as proof? Auspicious vapors of the nine heavens coil and gather at dawn.
The four seas gaze in unison, honoring the model of maternal virtue.
Ascending the hall, he holds his staff horizontally and says: "To go forth in this very manner—like one who finds broth when thirsty, like one who finds rain in a drought—from where does joy come?
From where does sorrow depart? He strikes the ground with the staff and says: "The rustic elder knows not the toil of Yao and Shun. *Dong dong.*
Drums were beaten to sacrifice to the River God.

Ascending the hall, [the Master said: "Yesterday, together with Elder Mu, I returned from visiting Mount Zhong. Looking out as far as the eye could see, the fields were all planted and the sowing was complete."
This autumn the harvest has ripened; a full meal may now be expected. How fortunate! How joyful!

Furthermore, I pray that there be no more drums and war-drums at the frontier cities, and that everyone may play the melodies of Great Peace. The Master of the Hall asked, "What is the tune of this melody?"
Ascending the hall, he said: "One person appears and disappears within the realm of cold and heat, yet cold and heat cannot reach them.
Another person wanders freely beyond the realm of cold and heat, yet cold and heat cannot restrain them. Now tell me, between these two people, which one possesses the superior quality?"
Ascending the hall, he said: "To walk without moving a step; to speak without moving a mouth. Before the cliff of Shaoshi, why were all his skills exhausted?
After a long silence, he said: 'The kindness is so great it is difficult to repay.'"
Ascending the hall, [the Master] said: "The mind of the Great Immortal of the land of Chu was secretly transmitted from east to west. Holding up his staff, he said:

'If you can recognize its place of origin here, I shall strike you across the shoulders with a single blow—not sparing it even for myself. If you hesitate, I bid you, those who seek the profound mystery:
do not let your time be spent in vain.'"
Ascending the hall: Nine years at Shaoshi, a drum suspended awaiting the mallet; one night at Caoxi, like glue meeting lacquer.
If you understand it in this way, thirty years from now, you will be filled with shame and embarrassment. *Pang!*
Xie Jinshan ascended the hall for the formal discourse of his dharma heirs. Holding up his staff, he said: "O staff!

When raised, it is bustling and clamorous, churning the thousand-fathom surging waves of the Yangtze River. When lowered, it is clear and cool, pouring out a single drop of still water from the Lingquan spring.
Now tell me: is it when raised? Is it when lowered? He struck the floor once with the staff.
Ascending the hall, he raised his whisk and said: "This sutra is taught for those of the supreme vehicle.
If anyone receives and upholds it, they will accomplish the most rare and marvelous dharma; this is called shouldering the burden of Anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi.

Great assembly, the former sages stand upon the ground awaiting you—do you still feel your eyes twitching and your ears heating up? With the whisk, he struck the meditation seat and descended from the hall.
On the first day of the year, he ascended the hall: "Yesterday we sent off the old year; the old man Wang of the eastern village burned paper money at night.
This morning we celebrate the New Year; Old Zhang drinks wine while Old Li gets drunk. Light as Mount Tai or Mount Hua, yet heavy as a goose feather—to deliberate upon the Buddha-dharma."
This is the circulation of worldly truth; each and every one of them is simply as it is. As for the phrase, "The one who acts as the lord of the myriad phenomena"—how is this so?
Look at the time when the command is put into effect.
Xie Shouzuo, formerly residing at Shangtang, took up his staff and said: "This is the phrase shared shoulder-to-shoulder before Taibai Peak.
Since we parted, throughout the vast expanses of east and west of Zhejiang, north and south of the Yangtze, it has never been moved.
Now that we are fortunately reunited once more in the waters and clouds, we cannot help but share the wind and moon equally. He struck the floor once and said: "Were it not for Zheng’an..."
It is difficult to explain in full detail.
Entering the hall [he said]: "In this way it is easy; in another way it is difficult. In another way it is easy; in this way it is difficult.
The golden sun flies up onto the jade balustrade; blink your eyebrows and look closely."
On the eighth day of the fourth month, he ascended the hall and said: "More than two thousand years ago, in the city of Kapilavastu, there was a public case (koan).
Throughout the billions of worlds of the four quarters, in the lands of *āraṇya*, the regulations have not been altered. This morning, I shall overturn that precedent for his sake.
He then descended from the seat.
Xie Zhishi ascends the hall. He climbs the mountain of knives and grasps the tree of swords; both dark and both bright, he tears asunder and gathers together.
He rides backward upon Yangqi’s three-legged donkey and kicks through Yantou’s final word. Who is this person? Realize it right before your eyes.
Ascending the hall, he said: "The entire earth is a pure lion throne; all phenomena are the broad and long tongue.
To expound this Dharma, there has never been a moment’s interruption. At this very moment, who is the Vairocana Teacher? Who is the Lord of the Dharmakāya?"
*Ha!* (A shout).
Ascending the hall for the Summer Retreat: On the fifteenth day of the fourth month, in both the Western Heaven and this land, the four sevens and two threes face one another;

they further inform each other, saying: "From now on, after the retreat has begun, whether sitting, reclining, or walking, we shall follow the rules and observe the regulations, maintaining constant mindfulness."
Water-buffalo! Do not let it trample the crops or encroach upon the soil and water of others. Among them, one person clapped his hands twice and said:
"Lower your voice, lower your voice! Heaven has no partiality; it assists only those who possess virtue."
Ascending the hall, [the Master said]: "One is three; three is one. Where there is excess, there is deficiency; where there is little, there is abundance.
To those who can maintain this continuity, he says: "Bring forth a single phrase! Speaking on their behalf, he says: "Seventy-three, eighty-four."
Ascending the hall at Qingmiao Monastery, [the Master] said: "I recall that in the past, Dongshan Yuanzuo said:
'Every morning when I rise, I drive the ox of Moshan, support the plow of Dizang, wield the staff of Linji, and carry the spade of Yangshan; I plow the field of white clouds.
For seven or eight years, he gradually established his estate. While this is so, it is much like performing a solo variety act—one cannot avoid being flustered and clumsy."
This is chaotic. It would be better to let Guishan drive the oxen, Dizang hold the plow, Yangshan carry the spade, Linji lean on his staff, and Baiyun till the fields.
Year after year, they sit back and reap the harvest of flowers. Why? Because that family has its own fine descendants;
from time immemorial, the ancestors have never gone out the door.
Ascending the hall, he said: "There is a handle, yet no news; a spoon cannot lift it, and a needle cannot pierce it.
For nine years at Shaoshi, one could not see through it; standing in the snow and severing one's arm, exhausting all heart and mind, one still ends up with nothing but confusion.
After three prostrations, one stands in one’s place, and until this very day, there is nowhere to find it. Raising his hand, he said: "Wuyi!"
Ascending the hall, [the Master said]: "Whether you can speak when opening your mouth or cannot speak, both are the second phrase. Set aside the medicinal taboos and return to me the first phrase."
Master Xie ascends the hall to give a Dharma talk on the gift of a Dharma drum by County Magistrate Chen. "Take empty space as the drum and Mount Sumeru as the mallet;
those who understand the sound shall join hands and return together. Today, at Ba’en Temple, I too strike a single blow. (He takes up his staff, strikes once, and says: "Kai! (Open!)
Immediately, all the deaf were startled awake and their dreams vanished of their own accord. He struck once more: "It is not only Avalokiteśvara;
I too have realized it from within this. He struck once more.
Ascending the hall, he said: "As soon as you intend to act thus, it is already not thus. Without relying on a single blow of the mallet, you would still be the same as a clumsy failure.
But what about Xuansha’s lack of penetration or Yunmen’s ‘slipping of the word’? How do you deal with that? He struck the meditation seat once.
Ascending the hall at the conclusion of the summer retreat: A single leaf falls and autumn comes to all under heaven. Today the sackcloth bag is once again untied at the head.
On the ancient path not a single inch of grass has ever grown; why did Ciming travel to Fenzhou?
Ascending the hall, [the Master] said: "Because empty space is boundless, the worlds are boundless. Because the worlds are boundless, sentient beings are boundless.
Because sentient beings are boundless, the distinctions in their mental activities are likewise boundless. Holding his staff horizontally, he asked:
"Where are empty space, the worlds, sentient beings, and their mental activities? He drew a line across and said: "If you do not obtain the flowing water, you shall return."
One should pass beyond other mountains. Entering the hall: it has no head and no tail; it has no back and no face. To know it is to be separated from it; to turn toward it is to be far from it;

Like a superb falcon soaring toward the heavens, like a white-browed tiger blocking the road—dare any approach? *Ge*.

Ascending the hall for the summer retreat: ninety days of *an-gu* (sitting in seclusion), a sacred regulation established two thousand years ago; in every thought-moment, one is present throughout the three periods of time and the ten directions.
"Step by step through the ten directions and three periods of time—how is this different from being in a bustling marketplace? Baoshou’s true face is fully revealed at the butcher’s block.
Panshan has attained a secret resonance with his own mind. He gave a shout and said, "The local government has recently issued a directive:
no more citing precedents or seeking exemptions."
Ascending the hall at Qingmiao Monastery: If one discusses this matter, it is like a person farming a field. One must know that this plot of land is the ancestral livelihood;
one must plow it deeply with effort and sow the seeds in due season. If a timely rain is encountered, the sprouts will naturally flourish.
If there is drought, one irrigates; if there is flooding, one drains it. Thus one nourishes the spiritual seedlings and waits for them to ripen into grain. To the south...
Senshi Kamako gathers the harvest; Fuke’s flail strikes from head to foot. Having been roughly pounded and finely winnowed, there is Master Lu who rinses it clean and cooks it to perfection;
how could Xueqiao not provide for the whole family to eat their fill?

Forgetting a hundred days of hunger in a single meal, celebrating the feast as an act of gratitude is but a matter of daily routine. Yet, in the end, what was planted—was it rice or wheat? If you say...
It is all contained within; how utterly deceptive! If you wish for the definitive truth, simply remember:
"I would rather have enough money to keep my guests drunk than ride a horse past others' doors."

Ascending the hall, he said: "To grasp the ultimate meaning before the movement of the mind, the seas are calm and the rivers clear; to clarify the fundamental source beneath a single phrase, heaven revolves and earth turns.
To sweep away all obstructions depends on oneself; to establish the Way is not due to another. A-he-he! [He raises his whisk and says: Do you see? [He strikes the meditation seat.]”
A hawk flies over Silla. Entering the hall, he said:
"Sitting by the fire in the sixth month; having eyes but no ears. An iron snake cannot bore through; an iron ox cannot break through.
Ultimately, how is it? Having eyes but no ears; sitting by the fire in the sixth month."
Ascending the hall: Five days remain until the summer retreat ends. Is that matter settled yet? How could it compare to Changtingzi, who lowered his head and woke from sleep?
I cannot tolerate it: as the golden crow rises in the east and the jade hare sets in the west, when birth and death arrive, where can one evade them?
Shaking his hand, he said: "Lower your voices! Lower your voices! The walls have ears!"
Ascending the hall, [the Master said]: "The ancients and the people of today—whether they speak of it or do not speak of it, it is a matter entirely without a handle.
The elephant-king turns in circles; the lion plays. [He] struck the meditation seat and said: 'In the end, it is something one cannot even prop up.'"
Ascending the hall: Last year and this year; the eighth month and the ninth month. One tree, two trees—the vermilion cassias hang their branches in disarray.
Three branches, four branches—the yellow chrysanthemums reveal their secrets. Here, though meeting, we do not encounter one another; here, though encountering, we part once more.
Old Fenggan’s mind has not yet rested; he rides a toothless tiger, doing nothing but chattering to everyone he meets. Aha-ha!
North, south, east, and west—a single lump of raw iron.
Ascending the hall on the first day of the New Year: The New Year begins its reign; from a thousand gates and ten thousand households, all things are renewed.

From the mountains and by the waters, to the head seat within the hall and all the great assembly—enveloped by a myriad flowers—we pray that you each enjoy ten thousand blessings in your honorable state.
Like the bright pearl of the vast sea or the exquisite jade of Mount Kunlun, have you not seen Mahesvara?
This man has torn off his mask, baring three eyes; he is fit to serve as a model for devas and humans. Entering the hall, [he said]:
"If it is correct in one place, it is correct in a thousand places and a hundred places. If it is incorrect in one place, it is incorrect in a thousand places and a hundred places."
"It is and yet it is not. It is and yet it is not. It is not and yet it is. Of these two lines of speech, which one is primary?
[The Master] strikes the meditation seat and says: "Realize it within right and wrong."
Ascending the hall, [the Master] said: "An ancient worthy said, 'To be absent for even a moment is to be like a dead person. Now tell me, when one is not present, where exactly is one?
*Shout!* How excellent it is to be 'not present'!"
Incense is offered for the anniversary of the Venerable Yanshi’s passing. Ou-feng deployed an array of iron chains; I once swept them aside with my long sleeves.
Ou-feng cast a vajra-ring; I once shattered it with my iron whip. Where there was no enmity, I gave rise to enmity; where there was no resentment, I created resentment.
How shall I repay him today? Inserting the incense, he said: "To repay him, this is the supreme means."
Ascending the hall, [the Master said]: "The incense pillar and the lantern—these are what they preach for you all; this is the second phrase.

National Teacher Huairang’s long silence—this is the second phrase. What about the true first phrase? To attempt to study the profound mystery with the mind is much like heading west while facing east."
Ascending the hall at the commencement of the summer retreat: With the Great Perfect Enlightenment as my monastery, the Buddhas of the past shall not be judged with heavy penalties;
the Bodhisattvas of the present shall have no reason for unjust verdicts; and as for the students of the future—*tut*! Be careful not to roll about in the weeds.
Ascending the hall, [the Master] raised the following case: Zhaozhou visited a certain hermitage master and asked, "Is there anything here? Is there anything here? The master held up his fist.
Zhaozhou said, "The water is too shallow; it is no place to moor a boat. He then visited another hermitage master and asked, "Is there anything here? Is there anything here?"
The Master also raised his fist. Zhuzhou said, "He can grant release and seize; he can kill and bring to life. He then prostrated himself.
The Master said, "To say he can grant release and seize, can kill and bring to life—this too is merely being habituated to taking advantage of the opportunity."
Ascending the hall, he gave a shout and said, "Here, no such things as 'probing the tortoise' or 'beating the tiles' are permitted. He then descended from his seat.

Ascending the hall again, he said: "To take a step before the pivot, or to spring up from beneath a phrase—how does this differ from those who close their eyes when they fall asleep or open their mouths when they eat?
Is there anyone here who can skillfully discern the shadow of the whip?"
Ascending the hall, [the Master] said: "Directly beneath, it is still difficult to comprehend; seeking through words only makes it more remote.
He took up his staff and said: "You must not call this thing 'the staff. Is there anyone here who can turn themselves around and breathe freely? Do not run about recklessly."
Ascending the hall at the conclusion of the summer retreat: Last year on the fifteenth day of the seventh month, I went and went, yet could not remain;
this year on the fifteenth day of the seventh month, I stay and stay, yet cannot depart. To go is for a lion to turn its body; to stay is for an elephant king to look back.
Now tell me: what was it at the end of last year? What is it at the end of this year? If you can say it, I shall give you half.
If you cannot say it, I shall hand everything over at once. But what is it that I hand over at once? I hand it all over to the spring breeze.
Ascending the hall, the Master raised an ancient case: A monk asked Caoshan, "When snow covers the thousand mountains, why is it that the solitary peak is not white?

Caoshan said, "You must know there is that which is extraordinary within the extraordinary. The monk asked, "What is this 'extraordinary within the extraordinary'? Caoshan said, "It does not fall into the colors of the myriad mountains.
The Master said: "They cannot be mixed; their categories are not the same. The six lines twist and turn to reveal the double *li* trigram. Looking down at night deep..."
A thousand mountains white. Not one who is not among them would know this.
Mountain Hall: I have a word that reaches the root and the source; when raised it is incomplete, when heard it is not whole.
If you try to ask how it is, "Heaven! Heaven!"
Ascending the hall, he said: "I have a phrase that penetrates the present and spans antiquity; it is complete as both host and guest, and perfect in both its circularity and its squareness.
To simply accept it directly—this I do not yet dare to grant."
Ascending the hall, he said: "I have a single function that I hold up face-to-face. Even the spark of a flint cannot reach it; even a flash of lightning cannot pursue it.
Then, with his palms pressed together, he said: "Ei!"
Ascending the hall, [the Master] said: "I have one essential point that illuminates all myriad differences. Before the flower was ever held up, there was no need for a smile.
If you intend to ask 'How is it?', clouds will already be spanning the sea-cliffs."

Ascending the hall, [the Master] said: "I have a single phrase that is neither silence nor speech; it is already accomplished in daily use. I bestow it all at once. He struck the meditation seat and said:
"As before, one is utterly at a loss."
Ascending the hall, the Master raised the teaching of Dongshan Yanzu: "This summer, although the various manors suffered from drought and damage, I did not worry at all.

What I deeply worried about was that the hundred Chan practitioners in the hall do not understand the saying, 'The dog has no Buddha-nature. The Master said, "To shoulder the Great Dharma, one cannot help but be thus.
Even if the various manors of Baoen suffered from drought and damage, what reason would there be to worry? [But] within the hall, five or seven..."
"Brothers, you have all gathered here for the 'dog has no Buddha-nature' koan; I am deeply concerned about this.

Why? Because there is no place for cold in the cauldron of boiling oil. He took his leave and ascended the hall at Baoen Temple. Limping and dragging, staggering and stumbling—amidst that limping and dragging, he was like a spoon being lifted from the cauldron.
"Not so. When the [fire-]columns stood in rows, the *Yan Tian* heavens scattered snow for twelve years. He has resided in this place for that long;
the ancestral style of Yangqi has never been leaked until now—it is leaked today: the scale-weight was originally but a single lump of iron.
Record of the Discourse at Nengren Chan Monastery in Jiankang Prefecture, compiled by Attendant Zonghuan.
Entering the monastery and occupying the Abbot’s quarters:
the furnace that smelts gold, the mold that casts men. The single silence of Vimalakīrti; the three [instances] of the National Master.
"Ha! Although it is thus, where will you all search? (He lets out a shout. Holding up the document, he says: "Green mountains and white clouds;
the bustling marketplace of red dust. This is a settled case; when the principle is clear, it should be acted upon immediately.
Why do you not know it exists? He hands the document to the Rector (Vina), saying: "The official seal is clear."
He ascended the seat. Having offered incense and finished the prayers for the Emperor, he took his place.
A monk asked, "When Mazu ascended the hall, Baizhang rolled up his mat; what was the meaning of this?
The Master said, "It is not without a father that a son is born. The monk pressed further, "But as for Mazu returning to his quarters—what then?"
The Master said, "Do you see Master Ma? The student advanced and asked, "Xuedou says, 'The true command is not being exercised;
he twists the crooked to make it straight. What about that? The Master said, "He even has a bystander to testify for him.
The student asked, "If someone were to come out from under the gate of Nengren and roll up the sitting mat, how would you, the Master, respond? The Master said, "That falls into the second place."
The monks prostrated themselves. The Master then said: "When Mahākāśyapa closed his retreat at Magadha, he could not resolve it through seven days and three nights of contemplation.

When Bodhidharma faced the wall at Shaolin, he could not fathom it after nine years of investigation. It is like using a broken chopstick to stir the vast ocean; one simply wishes for the fish and dragons to know that water is their life.
If they know it, they know it—but have you ever seen it in a dream? Xingnengren [the new Nengren] happens to be walking along and brushes his arm aside."
I have taken these golden pellets and turned them into clay pellets, scattering them before you all. A flushed face is not as good as straightforward speech;
intimacy through the eyes is no match for intimacy through the hands. Is there anyone here whose hand and eye are both intimate? After a long silence, he said:
"If there is none, then today the new Nengren has suffered a loss."
Wuye (Five Leaks) approached Shitou and said, "If our words accord, I shall stay; if they do not, I shall depart. Shitou remained seated.
Wuye shook his sleeves and was about to leave. Shitou called out, "Venerable One! Wuye turned his head. Shitou said, "From birth until old age..."
"It is just this. Why turn your head and look back? Wuye attained great enlightenment and then snapped his staff in two.
The Master said, "Wuye’s question was like a fierce tiger emerging from its den; Shitou’s sitting posture was like a lion blocking the gate."
He brushed out his sleeves and departed, leaving people in doubt. Why, at the very end, did he only attain realization while among old women, in a state of "da-da" and "he-he"?
Have you ever seen him in a dream?
That evening, there was a small assembly for instruction. The mountains are distant and the seas are vast in this ancient aranya;
The moon is bright and the wind is clear for this old bhikṣu. The myriad phenomena and all that exists are but guests; Upon meeting them, who would not bow their heads low? Lufeng said:

"A single flower blooms, and the whole earth is spring. Why did the Ancient Buddha not take advantage of the situation? If you can penetrate this, I will grant that you are indeed a golden-maned lion.
"Simha," the Master said, "A-he-he! To speak in such a manner is precisely the 'guilty conscience of a thief.
This mountain monk is no man from Puzhou; I certainly would not join this association. Why, for several days past, have you been wallowing in mud and water?"
"Directly, the eye cannot see its own nostrils. Such lack of opportunity—does anyone have the hand to come forth and rescue?
After a long silence, he said: "The tiller, the rudder, and the oars are entrusted to those who share the same boat to cross over together. He spoke again:
Having emerged from the dust, one enters the dust again; do not debate whether this is heavy or light. Try looking at the clear mountain stream outside the gate:
its movement and stillness have always been equally pure.
Ascending the hall for the opening of the furnace: A season of wind and rain brings the cold; yet here, though the furnace is opened, it remains unlit.
I address you, all you masters who investigate the profound mystery: seek shelter where it is chill and damp. Thus it is said: "Rest! Cease!
Go to the incense burner in the ancient temple; go to where it is chill and damp. When the ancients spoke thus, they were like cold ashes trying to burn one to death.
[The Master] gave a shout.
He ascended the hall. With the official carriages and canopies crowded together, he has already expounded for all of you the inconceivable Dharma-gate. Holding up his staff, he said:
"Now I invite Old Man Wood to provide a commentary from beginning to end. He struck it once.
Ascending the hall, he said: "Draw the bow of wisdom and fire the arrow of resolve. Layer upon layer of iron walls, stack after stack of silver mountains.
Beyond that, even further beyond—that which penetrates one point penetrates all. But when suddenly surrounded by a million valiant warriors and three thousand swordsmen, how will you turn back?
*Du!* If the eye does not sleep, all dreams vanish of their own accord."
Ascending the hall: The kitchen faces the monks' hall; the triple gate faces the Buddha hall. Whether coming from the south or the north, upon seeing it once, everything is seen.
After seeing it, what then? The guest is the host’s own reflection.
Ascending the hall on the eighth day of the twelfth lunar month: Daylight was seen by night, and stars were seen by day; the color of Mount Sumeru was blue and yet blue.
To go about in such a manner not only causes one to lose their nostrils, but also loses their very eyes. Now, where does the fault lie?
The Yellow River is turbid from its source.
Ascending the hall, [the Master] raised the case of Fenyang, who addressed the assembly, saying: "If you recognize the master’s staff, the business of a lifetime of study is finished.
The Master said: "The ancients briefly revealed a mere glimmer of it; one could say that once this was settled, everything was settled. Today, Nengren shall offer a different deliberation.
He raised the master’s staff and said: "This is the master’s staff. Which of you does not recognize it? Since it has already..."
"I understand. You should maintain this well.
He ascended the hall and said: "The green ivy winds its way straight up to the summit of the cold pine; the white clouds drift indistinctly, appearing and disappearing within the great void.
The National Teacher has thrust his head out from within all of your eyes and turned his body over upon his eyebrows. If..."
Seeing this clearly, one finally realizes that the myriad dharmas are fundamentally at rest; it is only people who create their own clamor.
On the occasion of the Imperial Birthday, he ascended the hall: "The Yellow River clears, a sage is born; the Sovereign reigns over the four seas, nourishing the hearts of all beings.
Do you understand? From now on, the war-drums shall lie silent at the frontier cities; for eternal days, all shall joyfully celebrate Great Peace."
Ascending the hall, [the Master said]: "I have a great illness, one that cannot be cured by the world’s physicians. The words of the Elder of Mingxi are still ringing in my ears.
What kind of illness is it? It is an illness that cannot be gathered together; it is an illness that cannot be supported. Everyone has it—do not slander him."
One searches for the place where it arises, but cannot find it. Alas! Alas! The Buddhas are not ill; they are because they are alert and conscious.

This very alertness and consciousness is precisely the illness. If sentient beings were truly ill, they would no longer be sentient beings. Having once been a wayward son, I am particularly mindful of the feelings of a traveler.
Cao Shan may indeed be called one who recognizes the illness. Today, this mountain monk also wishes to meet Mingxi. He said: "I have a great..."
This illness cannot be cured by worldly physicians. Simply turn toward the Way and request to return to the Abbot’s quarters to rest;
then, let it be guaranteed that both the sick and the healthy, as well as the one who knows the sickness, will dissolve like crumbling walls and melt away like ice.

Incense is burned for the anniversary of Master Yan Shi. Upon the peaks of Mount Ou Fu, amidst the ranks of dragons and snakes, if the general does not lead with courage, he brings disaster upon his entire army.
From this point on, throughout Jiangxi and Hunan, things proceeded in this manner; across the mountains of Wu and the waters of Shu, all was in a state of tumultuous confusion.
Beneath the moon over the heavy city walls, amidst green mountains and white clouds—once you think of you, again you resent you.

When Chen Zhaopu, the Regional Commander for the Subjugation of Rebels in Jiangdong, requested that [the Master] ascend the seat to commemorate those who had fallen in battle, the questions and answers are not recorded here.

From the raising of the flower at Vulture Peak and the smile of Kāśyapa, to the wall-gazing at Shaolin and the nodding of Bodhidharma, since then there has been the single transmission of the four and seven patriarchs and the direct pointing of the two and three successors.
They did not consort with things or self, nor did they dwell in the same marketplace as the holy or the ordinary; they were silent, forgetting all conditions, and transcended...
However, this was attained spontaneously. Since the time of Caoxi and continuing through Jiangxi, they have clarified the great capacity and manifested the great function;

they have turned the seals of the Minister of Agriculture upside down and held high the sword from the royal treasury. Sweeping away the portents of calamity and exterminating rebels, they have purified the realm and established an era of peace.
Then, looking back at the assembly, he said: "If one can take responsibility here, one's efforts will not be in vain. If, however—
Or perhaps not. After the rain falls upon the mountains of Huai, new greenness is added; one suspects this is the General’s heart for defeating the rebels. Again, there is a verse:
A man of integrity who serves his country with a sincere heart— Whether advancing or retreating, living or dying, he already knows it himself. A hero who surpasses all ages—how could he fear death?
In a single moment of loyalty and valor, who else can equal him? The moonlit night at the General’s tomb in Yecheng; The spring clouds over Mount Jiang.
The Imperial Ancestral Temple. From this point at the temple below Longguang Mountain, Guige also inscribed a magnificent stele.
Regarding the Buddha’s entry into Nirvana upon ascending the hall: before the fifteenth day, the Buddha was born; yet the Buddha was never born.
You all, being here with me, must not give rise to a mind of longing or attachment. After the fifteenth day, the Buddha passed away; yet the Buddha was never...
"Extinction! You people here must not give rise to thoughts of longing for the past.
Right now, as the heart of yearning and admiration has vanished and the thought of reminiscence has also stilled—how should you act while staying here with me?
He let out a shout.
Ascending the hall on the twenty-fifth day of the third month: How much of the fragrant spring remains? A single path of ordinary mind.
These eccentric words and inverted phrases—do not say they are merely raising a hand to pluck the willow blossoms; who knows they are but the catkins drifting through the air?
Seize them with vigor while the light flows by! The porridge has been eaten; go wash the alms bowl.
Ascending the hall, [the Master] raised this case: When the World-Honored One saw Mañjuśrī standing outside the gate, he said, "Mañjuśrī, Mañjuśrī, why do you not enter the gate?
Mañjuśrī replied, "I do not see a single dharma outside the gate; how can you tell me to enter?
The Master said, "He speaks the principle well. He then offered this verse: "I do not see a single dharma outside the gate; On level ground there is no..."
This is simply burying oneself alive. If you are a true cub of the golden-maned lion, you must quickly shift your steps and enter the gate.

*Ei!* [The Master] ascends the hall: "Zen, Zen—ten thousand, ten thousand, a thousand! Eyebrows tucked into the temples, ears hanging down to the shoulders. Amidst the reflections of a thousand flowers, at the tips of a hundred blades of grass.
Sometimes driving a stake into empty space; sometimes growing a lotus on dry land. This draws forth the Cold Mountain Man."
A laugh that overturns the heavens. Having composed a couplet or two of new verse, he completes the three hundred pieces. *Hè!*—a shout! His habitual tendencies (*vāsanā*) still remain.
Master Xie Zhu ascends the hall: The green mountains are his home; the white clouds are his door. In this secure and secluded field, crows do not fly.
[He] crossed over. With a single turn of the head before the Drum-Belly Terrace, he realized it was already the twenty-fifth day of the fourth month.
He ascended the hall and said: "Chang'an is very noisy, but my kingdom is at peace. When the ancients responded to circumstances on a single occasion, they were remarkably extraordinary."
Having no way to emerge from the body, what can be called "my country"? Even when encountering a sharp blade, one remains ever serene;
even if encountering lethal poison, one remains ever at ease.
Ascending the hall, he said: "A ninety-day period has been set for attaining realization. Eighty days have already passed. Is there anyone here who has communicated a message of this matter?
After a long silence, he said: 'The strange beast hides its head and horns; the spiritual bird guards its feathers and down.'"

At the conclusion of the summer retreat, the Master ascended the hall. He raised the following case: A monk asked Fengxue, "The summer retreat has ended; we ask the Master to offer words of commendation for our labors.
Fengxue said, "Emerging from the mountain peaks, he brushes away the rain from the dragon’s cave; drifting upon the waves, the monk causes the flower to surge from his alms-bowl bag. The Master said:

"To discuss merit while begrudging reward—neither of these masters were yet true adepts. Had I been asked by Nengren, I would have simply said: 'Take well one drop of Caoxi’s water and scatter it as dew for all people.'"
After three days of continuous rain, he ascended the hall and said:
"A single phrase is like an iron stake; it cannot be lifted by Shaoshi, nor can it be shaken by Caoxi.
Those with skill may do as they please, supporting it from the left or holding it from the right; those without skill need not worry, for it is available for their total utilization."
He gave a shout and said: "Bapeng gathers at the wall; heaven is but a foot away.
He ascended the hall, struck the meditation seat, and tapped the desk: "The false dharma blazes fiercely; pointing a finger or raising a fist causes the True Lineage to fall flat.

To forget words and grasp the essential meaning is to remain stuck in dullness and deluded confinement. A single phrase that strikes the vital point leaves the palace and loses the throne. After all, how is it? He gave a shout.
“Ho! He ascended the hall and said: “A monk once asked the National Teacher, ‘What is the Dharmakāya Vairocana? The National Teacher replied, ‘Bring me the pure water pitcher.
When the monk brought the pitcher, the National Teacher said, ‘Put it back where it was before. The monk then...
He placed the water jar back in its original spot and asked again, "What is the Dharmakāya Vairocana? Yunmen replied, "The ancient Buddhas have long since passed away.
Xuedou said: "Yunmen says there are no traces. Xuedou says: even if one could point with one hand toward heaven and point with the other toward the earth, how could one avoid having traces?
Do you understand? 'The clouds atop the ridge peak are never at rest; the water flowing down the ravine is far too busy.'"
"Born. The Master said: "The ancient Buddhas shook the earth and emitted light; it is a pity that people simply let this pass by.
Even Yunmen with a thousand hands could not cover it, and Xuedou with a thousand eyes could not see enough of it. If you understand, the clouds are at the mountain peak;
if you do not understand, the water flows down the ravine. Do you understand? He struck the meditation seat and descended.
Ascending the hall, he held up his staff and said: "This rugged staff is neither long nor short. When walking east or west, exert yourself with all your might;
when sitting securely at home, do not concern yourself with anything at all. Those who exert themselves are my fellow travelers;
those who do not concern themselves are my companions on the Way. Now tell me, are these companions and fellow travelers one or two? [He] leaned on the staff."
He said: "A public case already established.
Entering the hall: The dragon coils and the tiger crouches, majestic and imposing through all time; the waters of the Chu and the Qin-huai flow on, ceaselessly.
When asked why, one says, 'I do not understand.'"
Ascending the hall, the Master raised this case: A monk asked Master Yantou, "A sharp sword cuts through the world;

who is it that can face it head-on? Yantou said, "Dark. As the monk was about to offer further words, Yantou said, "Dull-witted fellow! The Master said: "This monk, with a single stroke of his sword, intended to take the heads of all people under heaven.
Upon reaching the presence of Yantou, he first suffered a fatal blow. To this very day, he has not lived again."
Ascending the hall, he said: "Where one hides the body, there are no tracks; where there are no tracks, do not hide the body.
When the ancients spoke thus, they had not yet emerged from the nest. Now, on Mount Zhong we hold hands, and in the imperial streets we shoulder to shoulder.
Speaking in this way, have you emerged from the nest or not? After a long silence, he said: "Take it slowly."
Ascending the hall, he raised the case of Master Māda (Mazu) addressing the assembly, who said: "All words and phrases belong to the school of Deva;
take this as the master. The Master [Zhaozhou] offered a verse: "The jade turns and the pearl rolls—look with clear eyes. Where there is involvement, there is no involvement.
Simply take this as the master. He let out a shout and said: "A single sword leaning against the heavens—the stars and constellations grow cold."
Master Xie Zhuang ascends the hall: "A step forward, a step back; with the hoe, there is no room for evasion. Seizing one opportunity with another;
seeking advantage where there is no advantage to be found. Planting the spade and folding the hands—this is the work in the field.
This is to carry the spring water and bring back the moon. Remember these words."
Ascending the hall on the eighth day of the twelfth lunar month: atop the Golden Wheel Palace, one discards the heavy for the light; before Mount Zhengjue, one plays with the real and the false.
Taking the boundless void and carving a single aperture within it, one reveals the boundless void through that single aperture.

From the exhaustion of the great earth to the end of the future, all things sentient and insentient are taken as a single document and passed over. This is for those who will not be deceived by others.
They went together to the Great Hall, spread out their sitting mats, and performed three prostrations to see how thick his skin was.
He ascended the hall and cited Yunmen, who said: "I do not ask about the period before the fifteenth day; tell me a single phrase for the period after the fifteenth day.
[Yunmen] answered on his behalf: "Every day is a good day. The Master said: "The mountains of Shu and the waters of Chu, north of the Yangtze River..."
The Southland. Step by step, secure and subtle; thought after thought, mutually familiar. Three before, three after—before you even blink your eyebrows, it is already intolerable.
After all, how is it? Investigate!
Ascending the hall, he said: "A chilling, solitary wind cannot be concealed; riding a horned tiger backward, one emerges from the mountains.

Within the Great Tang Empire there are countless people, yet those who gorge on wine and dregs cannot be called back. If they could be called back, before a smile even moves, their fangs and claws would already be bared.
Is there anyone here who dares to stroke a tiger’s whiskers? He gave a shout.
Incense is burned for the anniversary of Master Yan Shi. He laughed at Mi’an’s cleverness and rejoiced in Songyuan’s clumsiness.

He swept away Linji’s shout and broke Deshan’s staff, claiming he did not tread in the footsteps of his predecessors. He further said that he "discarded three and released two," claiming he had no dharma to give others.
He also said, "When one opens their mouth, it is not on the tip of the tongue. Aha-ha! This old fellow has today been caught by me.
"I have examined it. Is there still anything left unsatisfied? "Calamity does not enter the door of a prudent house. He then inserted the incense and ascended the hall.
He cited a monk who asked an ancient worthy, "What is the Buddha? The ancient worthy replied, "In clear discourse face-to-face;

if it is not the Buddha, who else could it be? The Master offered this verse: "Towering and majestic, ten thousand stalks of hoary beard; Staggering and uneven, several thousand bamboos of emerald jade. The wind..."
Knocking at the moon-gate, the three autumns are cold; rain beating upon the thatched hall, the sixth month is frigid.

Ascending the hall: A single blow from Deshan, a single shout from Linji—when the family is poor, it is hard to prepare the vegetarian feast; when affairs are busy, there is no time to gather the grass.
"Seeing a discrepancy from three thousand *li* away—still not escaping the shrimp leaping but unable to get out of the basket. [Zhuo] strikes his staff once and lets out a shout.
He ascends the hall and says: "The affirmative phrase is cut away; the negative phrase is also cut away. A man who betrays kindness and violates righteousness—hears it said thus and immediately..."
To go in such a manner is still inevitably to fall into the eighth stage. Why? "The moonlight on the waters and clouds leaves no room for doubt;
the flowers, willows, and spring breeze are a village all their own."
Ascending the hall, the Master raised an anecdote: A monk asked the Venerable Elder Chen, "I do not ask about 'removing one layer with another layer.
But when one does not remove one layer with another layer, what then? The Elder said, "Yesterday I planted eggplants; today I plant winter melons. The Master said:
"The white crane in its cage has its mind set on the clouds and the sky; the fish swimming beneath the net find the Dragon Gate difficult to pass. This is the old man of Muzhou!"
People! Those who encounter [this] are like men carrying a single board.
On the occasion of the Dragon Boat Festival, he ascends the hall: "Today is the Dragon Boat Festival. I do not wish to emulate those of old who went to gather medicinal herbs;
I simply rely on what is settled and used in the present moment. This can both kill and bring life. What is that which is settled and used? He lets out a shout."
He said: "To go on just like this—even to exchange one's very bones—is not yet certain.

On the occasion of the opening of the summer retreat, he ascended the hall and said: "The summer retreat begins and ends; this is the ancient custom of Vulture Peak. Geese are confined by jars; fish are bound by nets."
He raised his staff, struck it once, and said: "The transformation of wind and thunder occurs in this very moment; as for soaring through the heavens and the Milky Way, why wait further?
Is there anyone [who understands]? He struck the staff once more.
Ascending the hall, the Master raised the following case: A monk asked the Fifth Patriarch, "The entire Tripitaka is a 'cutting foot' (a radical).
I wonder what character it cuts? The Patriarch replied, "A-ra-niang. The Master said, "Although the Elder of Dongshan spoke with a full-mouthed local dialect, it was nonetheless extraordinary.
Upon closer inspection, however, it turns out to be a phonetic transcription of 'lei-ge' (to cut/classify). How is this known? For in another land, one is treated as kin."
Record of the Discourses at Taiping Xingguo Chan Temple on Mount Jiangshan in Jiankang Prefecture,
compiled by Attendant Zu Ding.
On the nineteenth day of the ninth month in the second year of the Jiaxi era, the Master accepted the invitation at Mount Jing.
Master Wuzhun took his place on the seat and said: "The treasure of Master Bao is not a color such as blue, yellow, red, or white;
nor is it a characteristic such as large, small, square, or round. The Three Sages cannot discern it, and how could the Ten Saints know it?"
For this reason, you, sir, should also keep it secret; unless it is the right person, it is not easy to entrust it to them.
Today, at Shixi, without any deliberate arrangement or calculation, it suddenly appeared before me and was obtained without intention. Now that it has been obtained—
Nor do I consider this to be anything extraordinary or intended to dazzle others; it is simply what it is.

Yet, how can I deny that these thousands and hundreds of my disciples have long held their hearts open in anticipation, all desiring to see me once? For this reason, I have struck the drum to assemble the multitude.
With earnest and reverent invitation, we pray that you will ascend this seat.

From the place where the incense smoke rises, may you emit this precious light, so that our entire assembly may, by means of this light, behold this treasure and together enjoy its benefits, throughout the bounds of the future, never again to lose it.
Even though it is thus, there is yet one matter that cannot help but cause doubt. Or...
There is a certain witless fellow who does not distinguish between good and evil. He has come before the assembly and said, "Jiangshan! Jiangshan!
You must not use the property of the monastery as a personal favor for your own kin. My nephew must provide for his own expenses;
do not let it burden your old uncle. Fearing that others might have no one to rely upon, I write this first to inform you.
The Master held up the document and said: "He can be caught and confined, yet by this he does not stay; he can be called and summoned, yet by this he returns again.
Where, then, lies the point of confusion? Dudo held up the document and said: "The spring wind disturbs all, never ceasing."

[The Master] pointed to the Dharma seat, saying: "This is the seat occupied by the foremost teacher of Mount Jing of the world, around which hundreds and thousands of patched-robed disciples constantly gather.
All people throughout the great earth look up to it but cannot reach it. Why is it that today the new Mount Jiangshan enters into this one portion?
A favorable opportunity is difficult to encounter. Thereupon he ascended the seat. A monk asked: "Originally there is no mind that seeks anything; boundless..."
The treasure-trove spontaneously meets itself. Master Zhigong waves his hand from afar. A person atop Lingxiao Peak nods his head in the dark.

The student steps forward and says, "I have come here; I wish to hear the essential points of the Dharma. The Master says, "On the five peaks, the mist is dense; in the two ravines, the waters are cool.
The student replies, "I recall how the Great Being Baozang sent someone to deliver a message to Master Sida, saying: 'Why do you not go down the mountain to teach?'"
[The student] asked: "To transform sentient beings—what is the point of looking up at the Milky Way? What is the meaning of this? The Master said:
"The three stages must all be hurried along together. [The student] further asked: "Sanda said, 'The Buddhas of the three periods of time have been swallowed by me in a single gulp;
where are there any sentient beings to be saved? How is this so? The Master said: "A single push and it turns immediately. [The student] further asked: "If, at the very beginning..."
"This is my preceptor. I do not know how to respond to him. The Master said, "The sword has long since departed. The monk bowed.
The Master then looked at the assembly and said, "Do you understand? Five peaks stand steeply; the Double Path rises high.
None but the right person can reach it; only those who arrive there themselves will know. As I observe this assembly—thousands upon thousands of dragons and elephants—not one..."
It is not that those who have personally arrived are lacking. Furthermore, what difference was there between the true regulations of Vulture Peak two thousand years ago and today?

Can you discern and clarify this? Can you penetrate through it? If you can indeed discern and clarify it, and penetrate through it, then there will be no hindrance to the north and south of the Yangtze, or the east and west of Zhejiang—wherever the rugged terrain is laid out and the perilous divisions are made, wherever the borders are expanded and the lands are reclaimed. Yet, suddenly, you are blocked by Jingshan’s refusal to let you pass.

"What about when the time has passed? [The Master] replied, "When we meet, one does not dismount; each goes their own way toward the future. The exchange of words is not recorded here. He spoke again:

"Just now, the Venerable Uncle on the Dharma seat pointed out the treasure of Master Baogong’s mountain-treasure and entrusted it to the assembly, ordering that this light of the treasure be released to make offerings to the great multitude.
It is hoped that by means of this light, you may come to behold this treasure. Thus he brought it forth.
Illumination and function manifest together; bestowing and withholding proceed in tandem. Not a single point can be hidden from everyone;
within the sphere of each person’s own experience—whether in speech or silence, movement or stillness—it turns and rolls incessantly. Can it ever be hidden even from the Abbot? Not a single point.

It may be said that this jewel emits light, reflecting and illuminating one another. Were I to instruct my younger nephew otherwise, it would be like placing a head upon a head; he could not avoid violating the communal property.

Suppose someone were to emerge from under the gate of Jingshan and say slowly: "To emit such radiance is all mere talk; where, after all, does the treasure reside?
How then would you respond? After a long silence, he said: "In the end, you have provided a mistaken commentary."

Upon entering the monastery and taking his seat in the abbot’s quarters, he looked over the assembly and said: "I, this mountain monk, have already poured out one ladle and two ladles upon all of you.
Those who knit their brows and turn back immediately will receive a blow right under their own heels.
If, however, you hesitate, wait until the Dragon Peak nods its head for you, and I shall explain it all for you."
[The Master] holds up the notice and says: "In the family of patch-robed monks, our nostrils usually point toward the heavens;
we go and stay as we please. Why is it that we are suddenly twisted around by this? [He] hands over the notice, saying: 'I trouble the Rector to clear my name for me.'"
The Master ascended the seat.
Having offered incense to pray for the Emperor and taken his place, a monk asked: "I recall that when Baoshou opened the hall, Sansheng pushed forward a monk;
what was the intent of this? The Master said: "Gold is tested by fire. The monk pressed further: "When Baoshou struck him, what was that about? The Master—

they will blind the eyes of the entire city of Zhenzhou. The Master said, "If one acts for others, one must act thoroughly.
Jin asked, "Baoshou threw down his staff and returned to his quarters—how about that? The Master said, "The path of the elephant king."
[The Master] cut off the fox’s tracks. The monk stepped forward and said, “New Jiangshan opens the hall today; what instruction do you have to bestow?
The Master said, “The staff has not yet reached you—it is for you to eat. The monk said, “It may be said that from ancient times to the present, nothing has ever fallen;
it is clearly right before one’s eyes. The Master said, “I let this one move pass. The monk bowed. The Master then said, “One barrier of Yuanwu is entirely without a path of approval. He holds...”
If you fixate, clouds will hang across the peaks and mountains will stand like pillars; there will be no room for even a glance. If you let go, the earth opens and the heavens part;
there is scope for the body to stretch out. This is still what is commonly used by all quarters. You must know that there is further letting go within fixing, and fixing within letting go.
There is a path through the profound depths, yet those who arrive are still lost. When one lets go within fixing, the bamboo doors and pine windows are filled with a serene, harmonious atmosphere.
With the knife and ruler at the tip of his staff, he cuts and tailors according to the occasion; within his sleeves lie wind and clouds—opening and closing are up to him.
New Jiangshan proclaims this: you all must not circulate it in such a manner. Why? The cliffs of Prince’s Rock are high, and the wind and moon are different;
only when you have personally visited once will you truly know. Furthermore, he raises the previous instance where a Zen guest asked about Baoshou opening the hall.
The Three Sages put forward a monk; Baoshou struck him immediately.

The Sages said, "To act as a teacher for others in such a manner will not only blind this monk’s eyes, but will blind the eyes of the entire city of Zhenzhou. Baoshou threw down his staff and returned to his quarters.
